brief: THIS IS THE BET. Take the swing — a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. In 114 iterations the town's material vocabulary has never changed: `tileKinds` (135) and `speciesKinds` (99) are the two census scalars that have never moved, and that is not an accident of measurement — there are 15 tile constants (`WALL 0` through `TUNNEL 10`, plus four) and 11 `SPECIES`, both unchanged since commit 1. #100's near block and #110's working roof were both built entirely out of them. Build the town's first GLASSHOUSE, on the allotments (`ALT_X0 78`, plots `ox 80..90 x oy 8..50`, `ALT_GATE 86.5`, the shed, `POND` at 90,49.5). It should be the first thing in the town you can see THROUGH: a new grid constant (`GLASS`) with its own ground and roof treatment, a low span you read the plot rows through, and ONE new `SPECIES` entry — a tender crop, `veg`, sown only inside, so it keeps ripening when `bloomCap()` drops on the open plots outside. Wire it into what exists rather than beside it: `snowAt` lies on it, `wetF` beads on it, `windowLit`/`LIT_PANES` light it on a winter evening, `mistAt` hazes it, and `spawnAllotAgent`/`sendToPlot`/`ripePlots` treat its rows as plots so the block's own people work it. Why now: the allotments are the longest-untouched domain (10 back), and every other rung-4b this run has changed the map's extent — this one changes what the map is made OF, which is the axis nobody has moved.
successLooksLike: The census reads `tileKinds` 135 -> 144 and `speciesKinds` 99 -> 108 — both are per-snapshot counts summed over the ladder's 9 cells, so those are the exact expected numbers, not a hope — and the baseline is re-pinned with `--save-baseline`. At 1600x950 midday the allotment block visibly contains a building it did not have, graded by a difference image quoted as a ratio to a same-code control run. On a January evening the glass is lit and something is still growing under it when the open plots are bare.
avoid: Do not site it on the POND or across `ALT_GATE`'s route — `spawnAllotAgent` enters and leaves there. Do not give it its own arrival source: the allotment band (.48) already feeds the block, and a second source is a different brief. Do not draw the glass as a live composite over the whole frame — the ground is a CACHE, so the fixed panes belong in it and only what changes is drawn live. Do not add a second new species 'while you are there'; one is the claim, and two makes the census delta unreadable.
